name: Investor Residence Permit

requirements.blocker_text: Under Presidential Decree No. 114 (issued June 2025), foreign investors with a licensed project receive a renewable 1-year residence permit valid during both the establishment and operation phases. Licenses are issued by the Syrian Investment Authority (SIA), with the Supreme Council for Economic Development (both bodies operating directly under the presidency) controlling allocation of state land and strategic-sector access. No minimum capital threshold was confirmed in any source reviewed for this build.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain an investment license from the Syrian Investment Authority for a qualifying project.

outcome.duration_length: 1 year, renewable while the licensed project remains active

sources.title: Middle East Institute -- analysis of Presidential Decree No. 114 (June 2025): tax/customs incentives, renewable 1-year residence permits tied to investment projects, and the centralized licensing role of the Syrian Investment Authority and Supreme Council for Economic Development

SIMA Insights -- corroborates Decree 114's June 2025 issuance and the renewable 1-year residence permit for foreign investors during establishment and operation phases; notes no minimum capital threshold specified

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Syria). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to two independent tier-3 policy-analysis outlets analyzing Presidential Decree No. 114 (June 2025), not the decree's own official gazette text or a Syrian Investment Authority government portal (neither was locatable/fetchable in this build; the U.S. Embassy's own 'Investors Handbook' PDF returned a 403 error on fetch). GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE FINDING: the decree is widely characterized by these sources as centralizing, not liberalizing, investment gatekeeping -- both administering bodies (SIA and the Supreme Council for Economic Development) sit directly under the presidency, and one analysis frames this as enabling 'political actors to mediate market entry through selective approvals' despite the law's generous headline tax/customs terms. This is disclosed as a real, sourced tension rather than treated as a simple investor-incentive scheme. No minimum capital threshold was found in any source -- not asserted as zero, simply unconfirmed. family_can_join set false (not asserted true without a source) and family_can_work left null since neither source addressed dependents specifically.
